page.layout: One printed page (page 280), with running head at the top and page number at the top left. Its text is one column of running text, with two numbered theses (IX, X) set in larger type, two Greek headings (Ἐξήγησις), and numbered paragraphs I and II. No marginal notes on this page. A narrow strip of the facing page (right edge of the scan) is cut off and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: perque punctum fuum fingula linea medium circuli tangunt punctum: ita DEVS omnium centrum, qui unitas simplicissi-ma eft, actusque purissimus, fese inferit universis, non ob idso-lum, quia cunctis eft praesens, verum etiam quia omnibus a fe creatis, partem aliquam vel potentiam intimam, simpli-cissimam, praestantissimam indidit: quae rerum unitas nomina-tur: a qua, & ad quam tanquam a centro & ad centrum suum rei cujusque partes & potentia reliquae pendent. Ad hoc plane suum centrum, ad hanc propriam unitatem se colligant creata prius oportet, quam suo haereant Creatori, ut per proprium Centrum, quod jam saepe repetimus, centro omnium haereant.
Modo quodam universalis homo est, cujus usibus tota inservit natura: Coelum, Elementa, Meteora, Metalla, Plantae, Animantia.
I. Modo quodam universalis appellatur; quia o-mnium, praeter se, finis est; solus enim DEVS sui est gratia, omnia alia propter DEVM.

II. Theseos nostrae veritatem egregie illustrat Cicero lib. 2. de nat. Deor. Quorum Causa, inquit, quia dixerit effectum esse mundum? Eorum scilicet animantium, quae ratione utuntur. Hi sunt Dii & homines, quibus profecto nihil est melius: quod pluribus deinceps probat, qua de re & nos pluribus agemus, sectione 2.
Particularis finis est perfectio corporis naturalis, ad quam e naturae praescripto tendit.

page.notes: The scan is cropped: a strip of the facing page at the right edge shows fragments of marginal text and a heading of the next page. These are the edge of the neighbouring page and were not transcribed. The Greek heading after thesis IX is hard to read in the scan, so it is marked [?]; the one after thesis X is clearer. The paragraph beginning "Ad hoc" follows "pendent." on the same line and is read as one paragraph with the preceding text. Long s is printed as a form like f in some words (e.g. "Thefeos", "Caufa"); it is transcribed as s. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept.
